This article compares the demographic and clinical characteristics of patients registered in the DANIBD database across Denmark's five administrative regions: [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]], [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]], [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]], [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]], and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] [^src1]. Because the data represents a single cross-sectional snapshot from the 2025 report, no temporal trends can be established; the analysis focuses strictly on regional disparities in population size, diagnostic distribution, age, and healthcare utilization [^src1].

In terms of total patient volume, [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] is the clear leader with 11,750 registered patients, while [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] trails with 3,637 patients [^src1]. The diagnostic distribution shows slight regional variations: [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] has the highest proportion of DK50 diagnoses at 49%, whereas [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] share the highest proportion of DK51 diagnoses at 58% [^src1]. 

Demographically, the regions share a fairly consistent gender split, though [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] has the highest proportion of female patients (54%) and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] has the highest proportion of male patients (48%) [^src1]. Age profiles reveal more distinct regional outliers. [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] has the oldest patient population, with both a mean and median age of 50 [^src1]. Conversely, [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] has the youngest median age at 45, and notably leads in the 30-39 age bracket (21%) [^src1].

Healthcare utilization, measured by the number and type of contacts, highlights a significant divergence in care delivery models. [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] and [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] lead in the mean number of contacts per patient (12) [^src1]. Furthermore, [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] relies most heavily on physical (in-person) consultations, which account for 71% of its contacts [^src1]. In stark contrast, [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] is an outlier in its adoption of digital care, recording the highest proportion of virtual contacts at 42% and the lowest proportion of physical contacts at 58% [^src1].
